judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional notices clause; "deemed properly given when delivered" by fax or overnight service is workable though it lacks deemed-receipt timing for mail.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Company address given is Ajuba International's Michigan office only, with no address for Ajuba India, the entity that actually employs and pays the Employee under 2.1 and 2.2.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard withholding language, definite on its face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers only to federal, state and local taxes although the Employee resides in India and is paid by Ajuba India, a mild mismatch with the preamble and 2.2(a).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the ongoing provisions of this Agreement, which shall survive ... in accordance with their terms" is circular: it never identifies which provisions are ongoing.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: No clause elsewhere designates surviving provisions, so whether Articles III, IV and V survive rests entirely on this indefinite formula.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is definite, but the carve-out for "that certain Non-Competition Agreement of even date herewith" leaves the relationship between two simultaneous restrictive-covenant regimes unstated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Article V of this Agreement is itself a full noncompete, so the preserved separate Non-Competition Agreement and Article V may impose overlapping or differing restraints — a genuine whole-instrument question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Short and definite; "the Parties" is not a capitalised defined term here, but its meaning is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Parent (MiraMed) is given rights under 1.5, 1.7 and 8.4(b) though it is not a signatory, and this clause deliberately accommodates that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain Michigan choice-of-law clause excluding conflicts principles.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A ¶17 selects Michigan law in similar terms; the only friction is that performance occurs in India, which the clause does not address.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate counterparts clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The signature pages are duplicated and incompletely executed, but the clause itself contemplates that.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "benefits under this Agreement" is undefined — it could mean employee benefit plans only or every payment due — and "attachment" is not something the Employee controls.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.4 makes the Agreement binding on the Employee's heirs and personal representatives and 8.3 contemplates payment to his estate, which sits awkwardly against a blanket anti-alienation rule.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "disparage" is undefined and the covenant is unlimited in time with no exception for truthful or legally compelled statements.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Exhibit A ¶3 limits the Employee's non-disparagement to "so long as Employee holds Restricted Stock Units" and carves out statements required by law — a different rule for the same subject matter.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A narrow recusal undertaking; "action with respect to this Agreement" is slightly open but operationally clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4(b) contemplates his Board membership and 8.2 requires the Board to act on Cause, which this clause accommodates rather than contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "may be brought" reads as permissive while the same sentence has each party consent to jurisdiction and waive venue objections — the classic permissive-versus-mandatory forum clause ambiguity, compounded by "against any of parties."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: With an Indian-resident employee, an Indian employing entity and Michigan law under 9.10, whether this clause forecloses suit elsewhere is a question that can only be answered against the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The recitals are a form with blanks unfilled and garbled text ("employment at band separation from Comnipany"), and recital C is mislabelled onto recital B's line.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Recital D says the parties release "any and all claims" while ¶1 excludes claims to compel payments due under the Employment Agreement — a recital pointing further than the operative release.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long enumerated statute list introduced by "including, but not limited to" and closed by "any other claims," with the carve-out "excluding only those to compel the payment of amounts due" — general-versus-specific scope is squarely in issue.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out preserves Employment Agreement payment claims while ¶19 releases the Company from remaining obligations on any violation, so the release and the forfeiture clause pull against each other.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Very broad list of property closed with "all other assets, materials and information of any kind or nature ... pertaining to Company," an open-ended catch-all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It substantially duplicates Sections 3.2 and 4.2 of the Agreement without stating which controls, but the obligations point the same way.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The covenant is conditioned on "so long as Employee holds Restricted Stock Units," a concept found nowhere in the instrument, and it assumes the Employee's departure was a "resignation."
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 9.13 imposes a mutual, unconditional and perpetual non-disparagement duty, which this RSU-limited version contradicts.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "To never seek or accept employment with Company" is a bare infinitive fragment with no subject or promissory verb, a mechanical defect that clouds whether it is a covenant at all.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is inconsistent with ¶6, which obliges the Employee to provide continuing assistance and consultative advice to the Company after separation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain acknowledgment that the restrictive covenants survive.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It confirms Articles III, IV and V continue, which harmonises with Section 9.7's otherwise indefinite survival clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "reasonable notice," "a reasonable amount of the Employee's time" and reimbursement of "lost wages" are soft standards, but of an ordinary kind.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It obliges continued cooperation while ¶4 bars any employment relationship and ¶1 releases all claims, a mild but noticeable strain.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short factual acknowledgment with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the release in ¶1 to which it cross-refers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard ADEA acknowledgment; it recites that counsel was in fact consulted, which may not be true, but the wording is clear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Fits the 21-day and 7-day OWBPA machinery in ¶¶9 and 10.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A definite 21-day consideration period.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It coheres with ¶¶8 and 10, though nothing in Section 8.4 of the Agreement gives the Employee that time before severance is conditioned on signature.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The addressee and hand-delivery details are left blank, so the mechanism for effective revocation cannot be performed as written.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 conditions severance on "execution without revocation" of this Release, so the unfilled blanks bear directly on when the payment obligation arises.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "the Company's obligations" is unqualified — it could mean only severance or every obligation the Company owes — and the heading refers to severance payments while the text does not.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4 conditions only the severance payment on the Release, so reading this as conditioning all Company obligations would conflict with the Agreement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Boilerplate voluntariness and no-reliance acknowledgment.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with ¶¶8, 9 and 15.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The Company's side reads oddly — it "agrees to disclose the terms of this Agreement only for legitimate business purposes" — and "legitimate business purposes" is undefined.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 3.3 of the Agreement uses the same elastic phrase for the Employment Agreement, so the instrument is consistent even if the phrase is vague.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One-sentence non-admission clause with nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It does not conflict with any operative term.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "regarding the matters set forth herein" is a limited integration formula, and the comma splice before "Any modification" is a minor slip.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It sits against ¶¶1 and 5 and Section 9.8, which preserve the Employment Agreement and the separate Non-Competition Agreement; whether this integration disturbs them is arguable but ¶5 resolves most of it.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Standard unknown-claims acknowledgment; the wording is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It reinforces the "known or unknown" language of ¶1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Ordinary Michigan choice-of-law clause.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 9.10, though this Release contains no venue clause corresponding to Section 9.15.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A reformation-style severability clause, long but internally coherent.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It differs in approach from Section 9.2 of the Agreement (excision rather than reformation), but each governs its own instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It releases the Company from obligations "under the Severance Agreement," a term used nowhere else — this document is the "Release" — and the sentence ends with a comma, leaving it unfinished.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The forfeiture also collides with ¶1's carve-out preserving the Employee's right to compel amounts due under the Employment Agreement and with Section 8.4's severance obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A duty to provide "recommendations" on strategy, closed by "other strategic partnership arrangements" — advisory and open-ended, so its content is hard to fix.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 makes Schedule 2.1 the controlling statement of duties and 8.4(a) treats diminution of them as Good Reason, so vagueness here feeds a live severance trigger.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "management and efficient operations" and the parenthetical "(including Ajuba US and all subsidiaries)" leave the reach of the finance/cash-management responsibility unclear.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 8.4(a) expressly provides that consolidation, elimination or outsourcing of cash management, accounting and sales and marketing is not a material diminution, directly cutting back the duties this bullet confers.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple reporting-line statement; "directly or indirectly" is standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.1's grant of the Ajuba India presidency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Four words, plain on their face.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1 says the Employee "shall report directly to the Board (or selected designee of the Board of Directors of the Parent)" — reporting to the Chairman is a different line, and Section 2.1 says Schedule 2.1 controls only over the Bylaws, not over Section 2.1 itself.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A concrete, quantified attendance obligation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1 and 9.14.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Employee estimates" the costs and the completion test depends on the "final day of employment" of three named individuals and termination of a third-party lease — events largely outside his control, though the test itself is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) conditions a $200,000 bonus on the UK office being "shut down ... in accordance with Schedule I" and pays it on the twelve-month anniversary, so whether completion by that date is required is contestable.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "Restructure" is defined only as termination of a named lease, while the narrative speaks of relocating systems and functions — two different measures of the same event.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) makes the Reorganization Bonus turn on the Novi office being "restructured" in accordance with this Schedule, so the mismatch here bears on a concrete payment obligation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It disclaims warranty by reference to "Contemplated Transactions (as defined in the Stock Purchase Agreement dated June __, 2005)" — an undated, extrinsic definition, so the disclaimer's subject is not ascertainable from this instrument.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(f) describes Schedule I as "set[ting] forth the specific cost savings for each action and a reasonable risk assessment," while this paragraph disclaims any representation about actual savings — the operative clause and the Schedule pull apart.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single, definite cost-allocation sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It allocates closure costs to Ajuba while Ajuba India pays the Reorganization Bonus under 2.2(f), a division that is unusual but not contradictory.
